summary: The Medicare Home Health Payment Integrity and Protection Act of 2026 amends title XVIII of the Social Security Act to target and decrease fraud related to home health agencies in Medicare. It implements new enrollment screening rules, increases oversight and survey frequencies for certain agencies, adjusts payment rules and calculation methods for prospective payments, and provides specific appropriations for program integrity, law enforcement, and state survey agencies.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to stricter enrollment screening, more frequent unannounced surveys, mandatory liability insurance and administrator fingerprinting if deemed high-risk, revised prospective payment calculations, and exclusions of suspect claims from benchmarks.
Impacted by measures designed to protect the integrity of home health services and benchmarks from fraud, waste, and abuse.
Receive dedicated multi-million dollar appropriations between fiscal years 2027 and 2031 to conduct accelerated surveys, investigations, forensic accounting, and prosecutions of Medicare fraud.
affected_groups.group: Federal and State Enforcement and Survey Agencies

key_provisions: Requires enhanced enrollment screening, including fingerprinting of administrators and comprehensive liability insurance, for home health agencies determined to be at an extreme risk of fraud based on rapid growth in agency numbers in a state or county.

Mandates monthly standard surveys for newly enrolled home health agencies, those with changes of ownership, or those reactivating billing privileges during the initial 36-month period, as well as surveys within 18 months for agencies missing quality data or showing aberrant beneficiary admission rates.

Increases the penalty for failing to submit required quality data from current levels to a 15 percentage point reduction for 2029 and subsequent years, while establishing a 30-day grace period for good-faith efforts.
Requires the Secretary to establish a revised standard prospective payment amount for calendar year 2027 using claims data that excludes fraudulent, wasteful, abusive, or unreliable billing patterns.
Suspends certain permanent and temporary behavioral adjustments related to the Patient-Driven Groupings Model for 2027 and subsequent years.
Appropriates $300 million for CMS implementation, $150 million for DOJ and OIG enforcement, and $100 million for state survey agencies for fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
missing_information: Specific numerical thresholds or formulas the Secretary will use to define 'extreme risk of fraud' beyond rapid growth in agency numbers.
Exact details of how the revised standard prospective payment amount for 2027 will be calculated beyond the general directives provided.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Medicare Home Health Payment Integrity and Protection Act of 2026 amends title XVIII of the Social Security Act to target and decrease fraud related to home health agencies in Medicare. It implements new enrollment screening rules, increases oversight and survey frequencies for certain agencies, adjusts payment rules and calculation methods for prospective payments, and provides specific appropriations for program integrity, law enforcement, and state survey agencies.
summary_detail.significance: This bill represents a sweeping set of legislative changes to Medicare home health payment systems and anti-fraud enforcement. By overhauling how standard prospective payment amounts are calculated for 2027 onward, suspending specific behavioral adjustments, and injecting $550 million in total targeted funding across federal and state entities for program integrity, investigations, and surveys, the legislation alters both the financial reimbursement framework and the oversight mechanisms for home health providers.

title: Medicare Home Health Payment Integrity and Protection Act of 2026
